messages:
anya: Heads-up: pushed rerank_v3 to staging with a sampling change (stochastic top-k sample of 50) to cut tail latency. Quick smoke vs v2 shows global NDCG@10 ~ -0.01 but a bunch of queries have high variance. Anyone free to sanity-check?
drew: Interesting. Is the sampling deterministic in the eval harness or only in prod? stochastic sampling can inflate variance of aggregate metrics. :eyes:
kai: In prod sampling seed is request_id; in the eval harness we were using a fixed seed historically. I accidentally left harness in request_id mode for the bringup run. That explains the noise.
anya: Oof. That would make runs non-comparable. The run logs show different candidate overlap per query. Need per-query overlap/Jaccard and CI.
drew: Can you paste the staging eval config? small snippet is fine.
kai: config snippet:
```
eval_sampling:
  mode: stochastic_topk
  k: 50
  temperature: 1.0
  seed_mode: request_id  # vs fixed_seed for deterministic runs
  replicates: 1
```
anya: For a proper comparison we should: (1) re-run with seed_mode: fixed_seed and replicates: 5 (bootstrap-like), (2) compute per-query Jaccard(candidate_set_v2, candidate_set_v3), (3) report 95% CI on NDCG and MRR.
eval-bot: Auto-eval summary run rerank_v3_vs_v2_staging: global_ndcg:-0.009 | mean_per_query:-0.002 | mean_mrr:-0.005 | notes: high per-query std. artifacts: https://redwood/evals/23456
drew: Also capture candidate counts pre/post sampling and topk overlap at rank positions (top1, top3, top10). If sampling disproportionately drops good candidates near the top thats a real regression even if global numbers look small.
kai: Ran a quick pass with fixed_seed and 5 replicates on a 10k holdout slice:
qid,ndcg_v2,ndcg_v3_mean,ndcg_v3_std,jaccard_top50
1001,0.612,0.603,0.006,0.78
2002,0.210,0.198,0.012,0.45
3003,0.845,0.847,0.003,0.91

kai: Observations: (a) many low-ndcg queries have large std and low jaccard 1 vs few high-ndcg queries with tight overlap, (b) average jaccard_top50 across slice ~0.72, (c) bootstrap 95% CI for global NDCG: [-0.012, -0.006].
anya: Thanks. That CI suggests a small but significant drop. Next steps: run targeted ablation where sampling only applied to tail queries (candidate_count>40 OR low-confidence scores) and measure. Also test temperature 0.5 to bias sampling toward higher-scored candidates.
drew: Agreed. Add candidate hash logs to the harness so we can diff ordering easily, and produce rank-wise displacement histograms. If ablation holds, we can consider a hybrid: deterministic top-20 + stochastic top-50 for tail.
eval-bot: Action items recorded: [kai run fixed_seed replicates=10 on full holdout], [anya run tail-only sampling ablation], [drew add candidate-hash + rank-displacement metric to eval artifacts].
